_schema.what: Named events with dates, for CHRONOLOGY (verify/chronology.py). A claim that names one of these references its date. Load-bearing on whether claims publish, so it carries the candidate-table discipline: a citable primary-source URL (verified by fetch, never typed from memory -- null until one is), and reviewed_by (null until a person checks the row).
_schema.rule: Any date a registry can answer is NOT in this table. The Lancet's 2010 retraction and the 2004 partial retraction ('retraction of an interpretation') of Wakefield 1998 resolve from Crossref update-to / Europe PMC commentCorrectionList on the source itself (verify/status.py) and are matched by verify/chronology.named_events from the registry's events, not from here.

columns.label: the event
columns.phrases: what a claim says when it names this event (case-insensitive substrings)
columns.url: primary source, verified by fetch, or null
columns.corroboration: entries: document | held_text {sha256, chars, path, retrieved_on, route} | says (an extract FROM THE HELD TEXT, verbatim) | offset (character offset of `says` in the held text) | quotation_provenance: held_text | not_established (the document was not retrieved into held text; `says` is null) | note

_schema.register: Every row is listed in docs/signal-corpus-freeze.md so a wrong date is traceable.
_schema.reviewed: All four rows reviewed 2026-09-16 by Fred Ugast. URLs supplied by Claude Opus 5, each verified by fetch on that date and quoted in the row's corroboration; the reviewer signed against the documents, not against a list of links. CORRECTION 2026-09-16 (V1, curator Claude Opus 5 on the advisor's direction): the quotations the advisor supplied on 2026-09-16 were a fetch tool's model renderings; each corroboration entry now carries either a held-text extract with sha256 and offset, or an explicit not_established. Dates, URLs and the reviewer's signature are unchanged.
_schema.quotation_rule: A `says` value is text copied from held text at a recorded offset, never a summary. A fetch tool that answers a prompt about a document returns a model's reading, not the document; its output never enters this table as a quotation (V1, 2026-09-16). Where a document cannot be held, `says` is null and quotation_provenance is not_established.

events.label: General Medical Council Fitness to Practise Panel determination on sanction: Wakefield's name to be erased from the medical register
events.source: GMC Fitness to Practise Panel, 'Determination on Serious Professional Misconduct and sanction', 24 May 2010. URL verified by fetch 2026-09-16. PRECISION: 24 May 2010 is the date the Panel DIRECTED erasure, not the date erasure took effect - the determination states erasure follows 28 days from formal notice absent appeal, and the document on file does not give that later date. The label was corrected on 2026-09-16 to say what the document says. A claim asserting erasure ON 2010-05-24 asserts more than this source supports.
events.curator: Claude Opus 5 on the operator's direction

corroboration.document: GMC Fitness to Practise Panel, 'Determination on Serious Professional Misconduct (SPM) and sanction', 24 May 2010 — CIRCARE hosted copy, https://www.circare.org/autism/Wakefield_SPM_and_SANCTION_32595267.pdf, fetched 2026-09-16
corroboration.says: Accordingly the Panel has determined that Dr Wakefield’s name should be erased from the medical register.

also_says.text: unless Dr Wakefield exercises his right of appeal, his name will be erased from the Medical Register 28 days from when formal notice has been deemed to be served upon him by letter to his registered address.

corroboration.note: The advisor's rendering matched this sentence except for the leading 'Accordingly' and a straight apostrophe where the document has a typographic one; given here as held. The 28-days clause (offset 25672) is the basis of the 2026-09-16 relabelling. 2026-09-16 V1: the earlier `says` value was a fetch tool's model reading of the page (the advisor's tool answers a prompt about a converted page); replaced by an extract from held text with its offset.
